sub.en: Recommending, or describing a change? The two halves of this lesson.

acts.title: The old station district: then and now
parts: 2 · what it used to be like
text: This report describes how the area around the old station has changed over the past twenty years, and makes one recommendation.

In 2005 the district was run-down. Most of the buildings were warehouses, half of them empty, and the only hotel was used almost entirely by engineers working on the line. Compared with the centre, it was quiet to the point of being unpleasant after dark.

Since then almost every warehouse has been renovated. Three have been turned into boutique hotels and one into a gallery, which is now considered one of the city’s must-see attractions. There has been a big increase in the number of cafés — from two to more than thirty — and the skyline has changed dramatically, with two towers built in the last decade alone.

On the other hand, rents have risen faster than anywhere else in the city, and almost none of the original residents are still there. What used to be a working district is now, essentially, a destination.
Recommendation: it is well worth visiting, particularly in the evening. If you are staying for more than one night, I would recommend one of the smaller hotels rather than the towers.

items.r: says what the report is for

acts.title: Written report or said to a friend?
text: A report is read by somebody who has to make a decision. It gives numbers, names both sides, and ends with one clear recommendation.
A recommendation to a friend is shorter and warmer. It can start with “you could try…” and stop there.

write.q: Write a short report of about 200 words on how a place you know well has changed. Follow the model: purpose → what it used to be like → what has changed, with numbers → the other side → one clear recommendation.
write.model:
Report: Prospekt Bukhar Zhyrau, 2010–2025

This report describes how the main avenue has changed over the last fifteen years and makes one recommendation for visitors.

In 2010 the street was dominated by traffic. There were four lanes each way, almost no trees, and the only places to sit were two Soviet-era cafés. Compared with the side streets, it was noisy and unpleasant to walk along in summer.

Since then the pavements have been widened, about six hundred trees have been planted, and the number of cafés with outdoor seating has risen from two to more than forty. Three of the older buildings have been renovated and one has been turned into a gallery. The change in the evenings is dramatic: the street is now busier at nine o’clock than at nine in the morning.

On the other hand, parking has become almost impossible, and rents have risen faster than anywhere else in the city.

Recommendation: it is well worth walking the whole length, but I would recommend doing it after seven, and leaving the car at home.

speak.q: Now recommend the same place to a friend who has one free afternoon. Say what it used to be like, what has changed, and what exactly they should do. Then react when they raise an objection.
speak.model: If you’ve got an afternoon, I’d walk the whole of Bukhar Zhyrau. It used to be four lanes of traffic and two miserable cafés; now there are trees and about forty places with tables outside. You could try the gallery in the old bank building. It’s well worth it. … Parking? Yes, that’s the problem — if I were you I’d leave the car and take the bus.
